alternate_names: Shri Dudheshwar Nath Mahadev Math Mandir
deities: Lord Shiva as Dudheshwarnath (Swayambhu / self-manifested Shivalinga)

history.dynasty: Legendary/treta-yuga associations; current math headed by 16th peethadheeshwar Mahant Narayan Giri
history.period: Mythological origins; Kaliyuga manifestation dated Samvat 1511 V (3 Nov 1454 AD); popular accounts call the linga ~5000 years old
history.summary: Shri Dudheshwar Nath Mandir is Ghaziabad's most famous Shiva temple, housing a Swayambhu (self-manifested) Shivalinga. Legend: a cow used to pour her milk over a particular spot daily, where the linga emerged - 'Dudheshwar', the Lord of Milk. Tradition dates the Kaliyuga manifestation to Monday, Kartik Shukla Vaikunthi Chaturdashi, Samvat 1511 V (3 November 1454 AD); popular accounts call the linga about 5000 years old, while Mahant Narayan Giri traces the shrine's founding to Sage Vishvava Rishi and the worship of Ravana and Kumbhakarna, describing it as a sub-Jyotirlinga of Kashi Vishwanath. NOTE: dates and the Bisrakh/Ravana/Vishvamitra associations are legend/tradition, not independently verified. The temple lies ~2 km from the Hindon river (Harnandi of the Puranas), the only Swayambhu linga near that river per local tradition. The ancient structure was renovated by industrialist and philanthropist Shri Dharampal Garg. The math belongs to the Shripant Dum Juna Akhara tradition and keeps 28 samadhis.

name: Dudheshwar Nath Mandir
town_description: Ghaziabad is a major industrial city of the National Capital Region on Delhi's eastern border, often called the 'Gateway of UP'. Its landmark Dudheshwar Nath Chowk temple draws lakhs of Shiva devotees from Delhi-NCR, especially at Maha Shivratri and in Shravan.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 38.5 km.
travel.railway: Ghaziabad Junction is about 2 km away, reachable on foot or by auto-rickshaw.
travel.road: On G T Road at Jassi Pura (Dudheshwar Nath Chowk), Ghaziabad 201009; well connected by road from Delhi and across UP.

visitor_information.best_time: November to February (winter months) for comfortable weather; Maha Shivratri and Shravan are the peak crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opening hours not verified from reliable sources - verify locally before visiting.
